subject: Post-call technical recap & mutual action items — Clearsky (inference SLOs)
thread_text:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.dev>
To: Maya Patel <maya@clearsky.ai>, ops@clearsky.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.dev>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.dev>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call technical recap & mutual action items — Clearsky (inference SLOs)

Hi Maya / Clearsky ops team,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and a proposed set of next steps so everyone is aligned:

Key pain points you raised:
- High tail latency during peak batch scoring windows (~99th pct > 1.2s for short prompts).
- Bursty traffic with unpredictable spikes from scheduled batch jobs + interactive UI.
- Cost sensitivity around per-token inference for high-volume embedding workloads.

Goals you confirmed:
1) Achieve 95th pct token latency < 300ms for interactive inference (95% of single-doc requests).
2) Support sustained batch throughput of 1200 embeddings/sec with < 30s job completion SLA.
3) Maintain data isolation for PII and ensure logs are retained for 90 days for auditing.

Technical constraints we discussed:
- Models: You intend to use an open LLM for chat (30B FP16) and a separate encoder-only model for embeddings (quantized).
- infra: currently on GCP us-west1, prefer VPC peering for Private deployment but open to Dedicated if control plane managed.
- KV-cache: significant reuse across requests (long conversational sessions).

Proposed immediate next steps (mutual action items):
- Redwood: share a short topology proposal that maps a Dedicated pool + private VPC option and quantization recommendations (attachment 1). Deliverable: topology proposal + cost ranges. Owner: Tessa. ETA: 2026-02-19 EOD.
- Clearsky: share a recent load test CSV (sample traffic by minute) and a short list of 5 representative prompts. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-02-20.
- Technical deep-dive: Karthik and Hiro to propose latency mitigation options (continuous batching config, prefix cache sizing, and multi-variant routing) and prepare an ops checklist for canary rollout. Owner: Karthik/Hiro. ETA: 2026-02-24.

Attachments: I pulled a small example topology sketch and cost delta table (redwood-topology-proposal.pdf).

If this looks right, I can convert the items above into a joint MAP in HubSpot and schedule a 45-minute deep-dive next week (prefer Tue/Wed).

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mailto:tessa_morgan@redwood.dev | +1 415-555-0134

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.dev>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.dev>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.dev>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 12:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call technical recap & mutual action items — Clearsky (inference SLOs)

Tessa / Hiro — forwarding Maya's note and the load CSV. Initial technical read:

- 95th pct target < 300ms for interactive: achievable with a combination of a dedicated low-latency pool + small-sequence optimized kernels. We'll need to pin a trimmed FP16 model or a 16-bit quantized variant to meet both latency and cost.
- For the embedding job (1.2k sustained): use a separate throughput-optimized group of instances with larger batching windows (batch size ~512) and async job routing to avoid blocking interactive lanes.
- Spiky 2x events: propose an autoscale buffer (burst nodes) + multi-tier routing that can shift lower-priority batch traffic to a cheaper quantized variant during peak.

Questions for Maya (to confirm on the follow-up):
1) Typical sequence lengths for embeddings (median & 95th) and average tokens per request.
2) Any regulatory controls preventing us from running short-lived KV-cache on shared nodes (if you require strict isolation KV must be per-customer).

I'll draft a short ops playbook this afternoon and attach a starter topology sketch (clearsky-reqs.xlsx) so we can align on instance types and quantization knobs.

- Karthik


On Thu, 19 Feb 2026 at 15:10:00 -0800 Maya Patel <maya@clearsky.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Karthik — the CSV has median sequence lengths around 120 tokens for embeddings and ~45 tokens for chat prompts. We can extract a sample of 50 prompts for you to test; will send tomorrow.
>
> For KV-cache: Clearsky security requires that any persistent cache containing PII be on customer-dedicated nodes; short-lived ephemeral caches for throughput acceleration are fine as long as they're flushed and not logged.
>
> Maya

2) Karthik/Hiro will produce an ops checklist and an A/B plan for quantized variant fallbacks and burst scaling by 2026-02-24.
